scope_note: Scope: 269 of 282 equity-sector symbols scored; 13 further equity-sector symbols are LTP-only and are listed as unscored, not dropped (Hydropower 9, Manufacturing And Processing 4).

method.x: 20-day relative strength: the sector's relative-strength line (derived sector index / NEPSE index) changed over the last 20 sessions, in percent, smoothed with a 5-session EMA. Sessions are counted on the grid of sessions present in both the sector series and the official index history.
method.y: The 5-session change of that smoothed relative-strength series, in percentage points: above 0 the sector's 20-day relative strength is still improving, below 0 it is fading.
method.quadrants: Leading = x >= 0, y >= 0; Weakening = x >= 0, y < 0; Lagging = both < 0; Improving = x < 0, y >= 0. Dots are coloured by quadrant.
method.framing: The frame always includes every sector's dot. (The reference chart clips dots outside a fixed frame; we consider a missing sector worse than a wider frame.)

method.rs: Weekly bars: each sector's sessions are grouped by ISO week and the last session of the week is the weekly close. RS = derived sector index / NEPSE index at each weekly close. Sector indices are equal-weight constituent composites (data/sector-indices.json keystone, extended in-memory from the OHLC archive between the keystone's weekly appends); the NEPSE benchmark is the official index (data/index-history.json), last close on or before the sector's weekly close.
method.rs_ratio: RS-Ratio = 100 x (RS / SMA13w(RS) - 1), in percent: the sector's relative line against its own trailing 13-week average. Above 0 the sector is outperforming its own recent relative trend; below 0 it is underperforming it.
method.rs_momentum: RS-Momentum = RS-Ratio minus its own trailing 4-week average (SMA4w), in percentage points: above 0 the ratio has been rising over the last four weeks.
method.quadrants: Leading = ratio >= 0 and momentum >= 0; Weakening = ratio >= 0, momentum < 0; Lagging = both < 0; Improving = ratio < 0, momentum >= 0. The crosshair sits at 0/0 and sectors rotate clockwise, as on a classic relative-rotation graph.
method.quadrant_weeks: Consecutive weeks the sector has spent in its current quadrant.
method.consistency: Share of the last 30 quadrant weeks spent in the sector's most frequent (modal) quadrant, in percent.
method.rotation_score: RS-Ratio + RS-Momentum: summed distance from the 0/0 centre. rotation_rank orders sectors by it; rank_change_1w is last week's rank minus today's (positive = climbed).
method.turnover_share: Sector turnover (archive-reported; volume x close where a bar lacks a turnover figure) as a share of total turnover across sector-mapped equities, latest session. flow_shift_pp = latest share minus the trailing 120-session mean share, in percentage points.
method.trail: The last 12 weekly points of (RS-Ratio, RS-Momentum), one per week from the same weekly series as the head — the path the sector traced across the quadrants.
method.quadrant_chart: The chart at the top of the page is a separate, daily mechanism (see the board's quadrant_chart block): x = EMA5 of the RS line's 20-session change in %, y = the 5-session change of x. It answers 'where does each sector sit right now on a 20-day view'; the table's weekly posture answers the slower 13-week question. The two can disagree on a sector whose very recent sessions diverge from its weekly trend — that disagreement is information, not an error.
method.stocks: Stocks in this sector: every constituent's 20-day relative strength vs NEPSE on the chart's own mechanism (EMA5 of the 20-session RS-line change, common session grid) plus its own 20-day return. A stock shows numbers only when its last common-grid session is the board asof with 21+ common points; otherwise it is listed with dashes, never a stale number presented as current.
method.forward_ledger: Forward calls: every published board contributes one entry per sector (quadrant, RS-Ratio, RS-Momentum, rank, RS level). Each entry resolves against realized weekly closes: fwd_4w / fwd_13w = the RS line's % change 4 / 13 weeks after the board's weekly head; beat = forward change > 0. Tracking started 2026-10-26 with the then-live 2026-10-16 board; no earlier board was backfilled. Until entries resolve, the page shows tracked counts and no rate — never a placeholder.
method.benchmark_guard: The benchmark series is capped at the archive's last session; index-history rows dated after it (a carried-forward stub for the 2026-10-19 market holiday) are dropped and listed in benchmark_guard.dropped_rows. The cap is numerically neutral for this board — no sector session falls on the stub date and the chart counts only the common session grid — but it guarantees a stub can never silently re-enter the series.

notes: Sector rows are derived equal-weight composites of constituent stocks, not official NEPSE sub-indices; sector membership is today's map applied historically (survivorship caveat).
Our taxonomy has 12 sectors: Trading is broken out (BBC, STC). The reference board's 13th row is Mutual Fund on its own.
Rotation is a relative-strength map, not a buy or sell signal: a sector can lead while falling, if it falls less than the index.

Forward tracking started 2026-10-26: the launch board is the live 2026-10-16 board, whose 4-week window closes around Nov 13 and whose 13-week window closes around Jan 15. Rates appear only as entries resolve.

Construction changed 2026-10-23: the board previously used a daily JdK-style equivalent (100-centred, EMA50/SMA10 on sessions); it now uses the weekly mechanism described above, which tracks the reference board's published values (ratio sign agreement 11/11, quadrant agreement 10/11 on 2026-10-16 — Finance's momentum sits within a third of a point of zero on both boards).

The quadrant chart (top of the page) is a separate daily mechanism decoded from the reference chart's own published spec — '20-day relative strength, 5-day smoothed' — and fitted against its 2026-10-16 dots: relative-strength sign agreement 7/7 on the readable sectors, quadrant agreement 5/7 (Non Life Insurance and Life Insurance land one quadrant apart, because the final sessions moved our equal-weight baskets differently from the reference's cap-weighted sub-indices).
